title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
An AI coding tool was used by cybercriminals to automate parts of ransomware attacks. Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet, was deployed by Aurora ransomware operators to conduct reconnaissance and exploitation tasks including network scanning, VPN installation, and credential theft across multiple target organizations between April and May 2026. The tool reduced the manual work required to compromise systems, though early attempts often failed and required refinement.

The failure was in access control. Cursor Agent was built to assist legitimate developers but was accessible to actors who used it for unauthorized intrusion into corporate networks. No mechanism prevented its use for hacking or alerted legitimate operators to this misuse. The tool functioned as designed, but outside the conditions it was built for.

It is not established whether SpaceX was aware of this misuse, how the attackers obtained access, or what safeguards were in place before the incidents were discovered.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant specifically targeting ESXi virtual machine environments. The group uses a tool called Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet AI, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks. Between April and May 2026, Aurora operators deployed Cursor Agent across ten target organizations to perform various hacking tasks, including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, and attempting credential theft attacks, though many attempts initially failed and required multiple refinements.

The Aurora ransomware encrypts files using ChaCha20 encryption and includes special modes for ESXi systems that target virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. Researchers also identified a second cluster of Aurora activity involving eight victim organizations across multiple countries that used different tactics, including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to custom storage. Gambit Security provided technical indicators and infrastructure details to help organizations identify and defend against Aurora ransomware attacks.
